correctness.rationale: Every factorization shape with total prime-factor multiplicity at most three is covered. Prime powers and semiprimes are immediate. For \(p^2q\), exact identification of the small divisors reduces divisibility to \(q=p^2+p+1\), \(q=p^2-p-1\), or \((p-1)(q-1)=2\). For squarefree \(pqr\), exact pairing around the square root gives \(\{1,p,q,\min(r,pq)\}\), and all possible divisor equalities are contradicted. A cutoff-\(300000\) checker reports no mismatch but is not used to infer the theorem.

value.rationale: The question \(a(n)\mid n\) is a natural divisibility problem for an arithmetic function studied mainly through average order and generating series. The complete \(\Omega(n)\le3\) boundary is structurally informative: it isolates two prime-polynomial families, two exceptional mixed-power cases, and proves a full squarefree-three-prime obstruction.
